title: sender ULID stored as sender_msg_id, receiver assigns fresh ULID — correct idempotency design
description: The idempotency design (sender stores their own ULID as sender_msg_id; receiver assigns a fresh ULID as the local message id) is the right split of concerns. The sender's id is suitable as a dedup key because the sender controls its uniqueness. The receiver's id is suitable as a local record key because it avoids trusting externally-supplied ids as primary keys. A contributor might suggest 'just use the sender's id as the local id' to simplify, but that lets the sender control which DB row is created — a security boundary violation.
